# Marlowe

> Marlowe v10.19.0 is an open-source, browser-based AI-powered app builder — a fork of [Shakespeare](https://shakespeare.diy) — with a Nostr-native focus. Users describe what they want to build in natural language and an AI assistant writes, modifies, and deploys the code entirely within the browser.

Marlowe runs 100% client-side. There is no server storing your projects or credentials. All project files live in the browser's IndexedDB via LightningFS, AI provider keys are stored in localStorage, and Git operations run through isomorphic-git. The only backend services involved are the AI providers the user configures (OpenAI, Anthropic, Shakespeare AI, etc.) and optional deployment targets (Shakespeare npanel gateway, nsite, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare, Railway).

## What Makes Marlowe Different from Shakespeare

Marlowe is a hard fork of Shakespeare (https://shakespeare.diy / https://github.com/soapbox-pub/shakespeare). The two projects share the same architecture and most of the same codebase. Key differences:

- **Branding**: Marlowe uses a teal/amber color scheme instead of Shakespeare's purple. The logo is a teal quill with a cyan spark. All PWA/install icons are Marlowe assets (`/icon-1024.png`, `/icon-maskable-1024.png`, `/marlowe.svg`, `/marlowe-icon.webp`, `/marlowe-maskable.svg`), with PNG listed first because Android's install-banner/WebAPK icon extractor cannot decode WebP. The Capacitor Android app (`android/`) uses the same Marlowe launcher icon and name.
- **Deployment URL**: Marlowe is deployed at https://marlowe.shakespeare.wtf and as an nsite at https://47h1rs70oqaspur8bichfzalg0wnassb8d7tslfacl7hwyaxhkmarlowe.nsite.lol
- **Nostr-first**: Marlowe defaults to the Shakespeare npanel gateway (`npanel.shakespeare.to`) as the primary deployment target: the site is published as an ordinary nsite manifest (NIP-5A kind 35128) under the user's own key, and the gateway is then asked (NIP-98) to point a `*.shakespeare.wtf` name at it — so the site stays readable by any nsite client even without the gateway. Plain nsite deploys (root sites kind 15128 and named sites kind 35128) are also available. Old `shakespeare`-type provider configs and per-project deploy records are migrated to `npanel` on load, and sites published under the pre-gateway host can be taken back en masse (Settings → Deploy, or right from the deploy dialog when a held name is recognised). nsite deploys skip `.map` source-map files (development artifacts not needed in production), scale upload timeouts with file size, show a per-server Blossom upload report on the success panel, report per-server failure reasons when an upload fails, and publish the manifest relay-by-relay with per-relay acceptance reporting.
- **System prompt**: The AI assistant introduces itself as "Marlowe" and describes the platform as a Shakespeare fork. Projects built with Marlowe are branded "Vibed with Marlowe".
- **Opinionated build defaults**: the default system prompt requires new apps/websites to ship with i18n in six languages (English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch — including a language picker and i18next-native pluralization) unless the user says otherwise; mandates sane Nostr data practices (no sub-second relay query timeouts, streaming event fetching with incremental rendering); and embeds the exact list of available virtual-shell commands (single source of truth: `AVAILABLE_SHELL_COMMAND_NAMES` in `src/lib/commands/names.ts`) so the AI never attempts non-existent commands like `npm` or `node` — package management and builds go through dedicated tools.
- **Badge**: Marlowe ships its own teal edit badge (`/marlowe-badge.svg`) for use in READMEs and project footers.
- **Additional Instructions**: Users can add personal AI instructions (Settings → AI) that survive system prompt updates — unlike the editable system prompt which can be restored to the Marlowe default.
- **Status bars**: Two thin progress bars in the project view show storage usage and AI context window fill at a glance.
- **Extended protocol spec tools**: AI agents can read Bitcoin BIPs, Lightning BOLTs, Blossom BUDs, Concord CORDs, Marmot spec docs, Cashu NUTs, Cyberspace protocol documents (CYBERSPACE_V2.md base spec + DECK extensions like hyperspace and virtual spawn), and kind 30817 custom Nostr NIPs in addition to the standard nostr-protocol NIPs.
- **Nostr Settings Sync (NIP-78)**: upload/download all settings (AI keys, Git credentials, deploy configs, app preferences) to Nostr via NIP-78 kind 30078 events. All data is NIP-44 encrypted to the user's own key before being published — relay operators cannot read sensitive data. Available in Settings → Storage.
- **Economy Mode**: a per-project toggle (🌿 leaf icon in chat input, and in Project Details) that saves credits on two levels: it injects credit-saving instructions into the system prompt (fewer reads, batched edits, concise replies) AND enforces them technically — tool outputs older than the last 24 messages are elided to a short placeholder (the AI can re-run the tool if needed), and the step budget per task is capped at 25 instead of 50. Default preference for new projects can be set on the homepage. Normal mode retains all user-attached images; Economy Mode keeps the most recent user image message and replaces older ones with re-read hints. The three newest tool images are retained in both modes.
- **Thinking level control**: a per-model Brain 🧠 toggle in the chat input bar that lets you control reasoning effort on models that support it (OpenAI o-series, Anthropic, DeepSeek R1, etc.). Options: Auto (default), Low (minimal thinking), Medium (balanced), High (maximum). Applied via `reasoning_effort` API parameter.
- **fal.ai image generation**: fal.ai is supported as an image generation provider (Settings → AI → Advanced) alongside OpenAI-compatible providers. Since fal.ai is not OpenAI-compatible, it is called through its own queue API (`queue.fal.run`, `Authorization: Key` auth) with a configurable main model path (preset: `openai/gpt-image-2.5/flare/text-to-image`) and fallback model path (preset: `fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/text-to-image`) — if the main model fails, the fallback is tried automatically.
- **Bug fixes over upstream**: Several bugs present in Shakespeare at fork time have been fixed, including a TDZ crash in AppDialog, a `toJSONSchema` Zod v3 incompatibility, signer extension retry logic, and showcase author profile resolution.
- **Divergence-safe push**: `Git.push()` fetches the remote first and refuses to overwrite commits it hasn't seen (throws `GitDivergedError`), protecting against silent data loss when syncing the same project from multiple devices/browsers via git or ngit.
- **New Chat context carry-over**: starting a new chat (title menu, `/new` slash command, or the context-window warning banner) prompts the user to either carry over a condensed recap of the previous conversation into the fresh session, or start with a clean slate.
- **Multilingual UI**: the interface is fully translated into 12 languages — English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Chinese, Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo — selectable in Settings → Preferences, with automatic detection from the browser's language preferences (including regional variants like `de-AT` → German) when set to "System".
- **Dist download**: a project's build output (`dist/` folder) can be downloaded as a ZIP on its own — via the Download button next to Build in the preview toolbar, or via "Download Build (dist)" in the Project Details dialog. The ZIP holds the *contents* of `dist/` at its root, ready to upload to any static host.
- **Persistent image reading and visual history**: `read` returns concise image metadata plus real structured image attachments rather than Base64 tool text, so re-reading or referencing an image later does not degrade to a truncated-output notice. WebP/GIF and other image types are converted to PNG for vision APIs without modifying the original file. `region` supports cropped/enlarged detail inspection. Tool images are stored in session history, displayed in chat and moved to API-valid user messages at send time; the latest three are kept, and user images remain in normal mode.
- **Live file-writing preview**: while the AI streams a `write`/`edit` tool call, the chat shows the file's content growing in real time — an auto-scrolling code block with a blinking cursor and a live line counter (edits render as a red/green diff) — instead of a motionless spinner. A lenient partial-JSON parser (`src/lib/partialJson.ts`) extracts fields from the still-incomplete argument string, so the file path and content appear as early as they arrive. The code view follows along: the file tree refreshes automatically (debounced, preserving open folders), and a file open in the editor reloads from disk after an AI write — unless it has unsaved edits, which always win.
- **Offline PWAs for new projects**: the default system prompt and `AGENTS.md` require every newly created web app to ship as an installable offline PWA from the start — `manifest.webmanifest`, a hand-written static `public/sw.js` registered manually from the app entry point, manifest link in `index.html`, and an offline indicator. Plugin-generated workers (including `vite-plugin-pwa`) are explicitly forbidden because Marlowe's browser/esbuild pipeline does not execute Vite plugins.
- **Live build progress**: the in-browser build pipeline reports its current phase (`init` → `bundle` → `workers`/`assets` → `write` → `public` → `done`) through an optional `onProgress` callback on `BuildProjectOptions` and a `buildProgress` window event dispatched by `buildProject()` itself — so the preview's Build button shows a spinner with the current phase label (with item counters for worker/asset/file phases) no matter what triggered the build (toolbar button, file save, or AI `build_project` tool call). `done` fires from a `finally` block so the indicator also resets on build errors, and the button is disabled while any build runs. `useBuildProject` exposes the phase as reactive `progress` state.
- **Background keep-alive during AI work**: while the AI streams or a build runs, Marlowe loops a near-silent `sine.mp3` (~1% volume — far above Chrome's ~-72 dBFS inaudibility threshold, so the tab still counts as "playing audio" and is exempt from background throttling) with Media Session metadata (`src/hooks/useKeepAlive.ts`), so browsers don't throttle/freeze the backgrounded tab and drop the AI connection mid-run (important on mobile). The hook's callbacks are referentially stable (options via ref) so the 100 ms start timer survives per-token streaming re-renders; a rejected `play()` (autoplay policy) retries on the next user gesture; playback is resumed on `visibilitychange`/`pageshow` if the OS suspended it (an explicit media-notification pause is respected until the next run); and a teal indicator in the chat input shows whenever the loop is actually playing.
- **PayPerQ credits management**: when PayPerQ is the AI provider, the remaining credit balance is shown next to the session cost in the chat input (auto-refreshed after every AI request, with a delayed second refresh because PPQ bills post-hoc) and in Settings → AI. The provider dialog has a PayPerQ top-up tab: Lightning/on-chain BTC/Litecoin/Liquid/Monero invoices via the PPQ topup API, in-app payment via NWC/WebLN or QR/copy/checkout link, and live status polling until the credit lands. PPQ's per-1M-token pricing from `/v1/models` feeds per-request cost tracking, and HTTP 402 surfaces an Add-credits shortcut.
- **Syntax highlighting**: Prism-based highlighting for ~20 web languages in the file editor (highlighted layer behind a transparent textarea with synced scrolling, disabled over 200 KB; Tab inserts two spaces) and in chat code blocks. Token colors come from custom light/dark palettes (`.code-highlight` / `.code-highlight-dark` in `index.css`).
- **Leaner token usage**: assistant `reasoning_content` (thinking traces) is kept for display but stripped from the message history sent to providers, so thinking is no longer re-billed as input tokens on every turn. A per-project **Reasoning history toggle** (BrainCircuit icon in the chat input) can re-enable sending traces for provider/model combos that keep better context or cache coherence with reasoning included (observed with Kimi K3 via PayPerQ). Each request logs its token usage and the client-side cost estimate to the console for reconciliation with credit-billing providers.
- **Offline-first PWA**: Marlowe is a fully installable PWA built around a **hand-written static service worker** (`public/sw.js`) instead of a build-plugin-generated one — because Marlowe's own in-browser esbuild build (used for nsite deploys) doesn't run Vite plugins, a vite-plugin-pwa worker would silently never exist there; the static file is copied verbatim by both build pipelines. The worker caches at runtime (hashed asset names are unknowable at authoring time): navigations are network-first with a cached `index.html` fallback, so the app keeps working when the origin is down (e.g. HTTP 502); hashed assets are cache-first, other same-origin GETs stale-while-revalidate, and only `response.ok` responses are ever cached. After the first visit the client posts its already-loaded resources to the worker (`CACHE_RESOURCES`) to backfill the cache. A build-time `version.json` (CI: `scripts/generate-version.mjs`; browser build: emitted by `buildProject`; never cached by the SW) powers a fail-safe update check (`src/lib/versionCheck.ts`): any error (offline, 5xx, bad payload) means "stay on the installed version" — the app is never replaced by an error page. Updates activate only on explicit user confirmation (`SKIP_WAITING` message → `controllerchange` reload). A persistent offline banner with an install hint (`src/components/OfflineIndicator.tsx`) explains which features pause without connectivity.

## Architecture

- **Frontend**: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, TailwindCSS 3, shadcn/ui, Radix UI
- **Nostr**: @nostrify/nostrify, @nostrify/react, nostr-tools — full NIP-07/NIP-46 signer support
- **Storage**: LightningFS (IndexedDB-backed virtual filesystem), isomorphic-git
- **Build pipeline**: esbuild-wasm (in-browser bundler), Tailwind CSS CDN for previews
- **AI**: OpenAI-compatible API, supports any provider with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; fal.ai supported natively for image generation
- **Deployment**: Shakespeare npanel gateway (nsite + NIP-98 hostname claims, serves `*.shakespeare.wtf`), nsite (Nostr/Blossom), Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy, Railway
- **PWA implementation**: static `public/sw.js` + manual registration; `vite-plugin-pwa` and `workbox-window` are not dependencies. Vite remains a development/CI bundler only and is not required for offline support.
- **Android CI**: `.github/workflows/android-apk.yml` builds a Capacitor debug APK on manual runs and `v*` tags, uploads an artifact, and attaches it to tagged GitHub Releases; Gradle takes `ANDROID_VERSION_CODE`/`ANDROID_VERSION_NAME` from CI.

## Project Structure

- `src/lib/system.ts` — AI system prompt template (Nunjucks) with Marlowe branding
- `src/lib/deploy/NsiteAdapter.ts` — nsite v2 deployment (kind 15128 root / kind 35128 named)
- `src/lib/deploy/NpanelAdapter.ts` — npanel gateway deploys: NsiteAdapter plus NIP-98 hostname claim (`src/lib/deploy/npanelApi.ts`); site reclaim planning in `src/lib/deploy/npanelMigration.ts`; per-relay publishing in `src/lib/deploy/publishToRelays.ts`
- `src/lib/SessionManager.ts` — AI session lifecycle, tool execution, streaming
- `src/lib/chatContextCarryOver.ts` — builds a condensed recap of a chat's messages for new-chat context carry-over
- `src/lib/zipExport.ts` — `downloadFolderAsZip()`: zips the contents of a VFS folder (at the ZIP root) and triggers a browser download; used for project export and dist download
- `src/lib/partialJson.ts` — `parsePartialJsonObject()`: lenient parser that extracts fields from still-streaming (truncated) tool-call argument JSON, including unterminated strings; powers the live file-writing preview in `ToolCallDisplay`
- `src/lib/ppq.ts` — PayPerQ API client helpers: provider detection, credit balance, topup invoice creation and status polling
- `src/lib/syntaxHighlight.ts` — Prism setup (language registry, extension mapping, `highlightCode()`/`highlightFile()`)
- `src/lib/versionCheck.ts` — fail-safe version comparison for PWA updates (fetch `/version.json`, never throws; never reports an update when the running bundle has no baked-in version, i.e. `UNKNOWN_VERSION` '0.0.0'). Browser builds bake the project's real `import.meta.env.VERSION`/`BUILD_DATE`; builds invoked by Marlowe emit fresh `version.json` with the host app's version and the current build timestamp, avoiding perpetual false update prompts after redeploying Marlowe itself.
- `public/sw.js` — hand-written service worker (runtime caching; network-first navigations with cache fallback; cache-first hashed assets; version.json never cached; SKIP_WAITING/CACHE_RESOURCES message API)
- `src/lib/registerSW.ts` — service worker registration, prompt-based update flow (`onSWUpdate`/`applySWUpdate`), first-visit cache backfill
- `src/components/PWAUpdatePrompt.tsx` — update prompt (waiting SW + version.json check); activates a waiting SW on user confirmation, otherwise reloads the page to pick up the new version (navigations are network-first; sw.js bytes never change between app versions so `registration.update()` alone can't deliver them)
- `src/components/OfflineIndicator.tsx` — persistent offline banner with PWA install hint, "back online" toast
- `scripts/generate-version.mjs` — build-time `public/version.json` generator (version, commit, build date)
- `src/components/PPQCreditsContent.tsx` — PayPerQ balance + crypto top-up tab in the AI provider config dialog
- `src/hooks/useSendReasoning.ts` — per-project "send reasoning history" toggle (persisted in `.git/shakespeare/settings.json`, read per generation step)
- `src/components/NewChatDialog.tsx` — confirmation dialog for starting a new chat, with "Start Fresh" / "Carry Over Context" choices
- `src/components/Shakespeare/` — Core UI: ChatPane, PreviewPane, FileEditor, FileTree
- `src/components/StatusBars.tsx` — Storage + context window progress bars
- `src/hooks/useAppSubmissions.ts` — Homepage app showcase (kind 31990, NIP-89)
- `src/hooks/useAuthor.ts` — Nostr kind 0 profile resolution
- `public/marlowe.svg` — App icon (teal quill)
- `public/marlowe-badge.svg` — "Edit with Marlowe" badge (teal, ✒️)
- `public/badge.svg` — "Edit with Shakespeare" badge (purple, 🎭)
- `public/llms.txt` — This file
- `README.md` — Marlowe project README (features, how it works, mirrors) with both "Edit with Shakespeare" and "Edit with Marlowe" clone badges

## Nostr Integration

Marlowe is deeply integrated with the Nostr protocol:

- **Login**: NIP-07 browser extension, NIP-46 remote signer (bunker/QR), or nsec import
- **Git**: ngit (NIP-34) for decentralised repository hosting via nostr:// URIs
- **Deployment**: nsite (NIP-5A) for decentralised static website hosting on Blossom servers
- **App publishing**: NIP-89 kind 31990 app descriptor events
- **Payments**: NIP-57 zaps, NWC (Nostr Wallet Connect) for Lightning payments
- **App showcase**: NIP-89 kind 31990 events curated via NIP-51 follow sets

## Default Relays

- wss://relay.ditto.pub (read/write)
- wss://relay.damus.io (read/write)
- wss://relay.primal.net (read/write)
- wss://purplepag.es (read-only — profile relay for kind 0 resolution)
